target_customer: Government and defense buyers such as program offices, special operations units and labs evaluating multi-domain unmanned systems
problem: Mine detection and coastal inspection need both air speed and underwater stealth, which normally requires separate vehicles.
business_model: Hardware sales and contracts to defense customers for the Tempest hybrid drone
product_category: Hybrid aerial and underwater autonomous drone

founders.name: Joel Santiago-Baretti
education: BS Engineering, MIT (launch post says Mechanical Engineering)
previous_startups: Stealth startup building ruggedized edge compute devices for combat medics
founders.background_notes: IEEE paper on an underwater counter-drone solution per YC page.

founders.name: Alex Rice
education: BS Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, MIT
founders.background_notes: Published in IEEE OCEANS per YC page.

competitors.name: Naviator (Rutgers hybrid quadcopter)
competitors.what: Quadcopter that transitions from air to water, first demonstrated in 2017

competitors.name: Exail K-STER and REMUS class UUVs
competitors.what: Established naval mine countermeasure underwater drones, order for hundreds of K-STER reported

technical_complexity.rationale: A VTOL fixed wing vehicle with a pressure vessel that must transition between air and water involves aerodynamics, buoyancy, sealing, and autonomy trade offs that few teams have shipped.

defensibility.rationale: Hard engineering and defense procurement relationships take time to replicate, but the product is not yet fielded and prior hybrid drones exist as research.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large defense firms sold separate air and underwater drones; no evidence found of a competing fielded hybrid in sources.

market_need_then: Navies were buying mine countermeasure drones and testing multi-domain unmanned systems in 2025 and 2026 exercises; the company cites a 50 km range and 1 lb payload for Tempest (self reported).

branding.domain_note: Site kairoxsys.com, abbreviated name rather than the .com of the full name.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: direct, We make drones that can fly and swim

branding.brand_signature: Tagline We make drones that can fly and swim and the Tempest product name

brand_strength.rationale: Plain tagline is memorable but Tempest is a common drone product name used by Firestorm Labs and Tempest Droneworx, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Kairox Systems is a three person, all MIT, Fall 2026 hard tech company building an amphibious drone for defense. It is active with no exit and little public data, so the outcome is unknown. The key risks are hardware cost and defense sales cycles rather than direct competition.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom lists a 125k seed with no investor names (an AI generated profile that also gives conflicting headquarters of Boston and Cambridge MA); not recorded as a round. Founded year not stated. Competitors come from a December 2025 trade page and 2026 pages and are not direct amphibious rivals. Name of the COO is written Cavazos on the YC page and Cavazos-Cuellar on the company site.
